claims.text: Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 exhibits extensive primary non-eutectic phase formation during melt spinning at approximately 10^5 K/s.
Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 has a DSC crystallization onset temperature of approximately 600 °C when reheated at 20 K/min.
The proposed intervention replaces 2 at% P with B, producing Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P18B2.
Substitution of 2 at% P with B will suppress nucleation of primary crystalline phases during solidification.
Substitution of 2 at% P with B will lower the critical cooling rate for glass formation.
Substitution of 2 at% P with B will raise the crystallization onset temperature during reheating.
B addition will increase the viscosity of the alloy liquid.
B segregation at nascent phase interfaces will increase atomic-scale chemical heterogeneity.
B atoms occupy interstitial sites in this alloy.
B atoms segregate to evolving crystalline nuclei.
B segregation poisons the nucleation and growth of primary crystalline phases.
Atomic-size mismatch introduced by B increases packing efficiency in the undercooled liquid.
More efficient liquid packing enables deeper supercooling before crystallization.
The B-modified alloy will achieve full amorphous retention at a critical cooling rate of approximately 10^4 K/s, at least one order of magnitude below the stated baseline.
At a DSC heating rate of 20 K/min, the B-modified alloy will have a crystallization onset at least 20 °C above that of the undoped alloy.
The undoped alloy has a critical cooling rate of approximately 10^5 K/s.
The beneficial effect of B remains robust down to a cooling rate of 10^4 K/s and during reheating at 20 K/min.
Analogous FeCoNiP-B systems provide a basis for the projected effect.

contradictions.description: The initial-state field reports extensive primary crystalline phase formation at approximately 10^5 K/s, while the baseline labels approximately 10^5 K/s as the critical cooling rate for glass formation. If the latter means full glass formation, these statements are inconsistent unless the cooling-rate estimate or definition of critical cooling rate is clarified.

The predicted outcome is full amorphous retention at 10^4 K/s, but the experiment does not falsify that claim when the measured amorphous fraction is between 80% and less than 100%. Thus, its acceptance threshold is weaker than the stated outcome.
